exp: i runs 1..9. The IF fires for multiples of 3 in that range: i = 3, 6, 9. c is incremented on those 3 passes and printed as 3.
questions.q:
What is printed?
SET c = 0
SET i = 1
WHILE i < 10
  IF i MOD 3 = 0 THEN
    SET c = c + 1
  ENDIF
  SET i = i + 1
ENDWHILE
PRINT c

exp: p halves each pass: 10 → 5 → 2 → 1, each satisfying p > 1. At p = 1 the check 1 > 1 is false, so the loop stops. The final p printed is 1.
questions.q:
What is the final value printed?
SET p = 10
WHILE p > 1
  SET p = p DIV 2
ENDWHILE
PRINT p

exp: Each pass removes one digit with n = n DIV 10: 4567 → 456 → 45 → 4 → 0. The counter c increments per pass, tallying 4 digits. When n = 0 the check fails and c prints as 4.
questions.q:
How many digits does the number have? (count by loop)
SET n = 4567
SET c = 0
WHILE n > 0
  SET c = c + 1
  SET n = n DIV 10
ENDWHILE
PRINT c

exp: rev rebuilds the number backwards: n = 365 → rev = 0*10+5 = 5, n = 36; rev = 5*10+6 = 56, n = 3; rev = 56*10+3 = 563, n = 0. So 365 reverses to 563.
questions.q:
What is printed? (digit reversal)
SET n = 365
SET rev = 0
WHILE n > 0
  SET rev = rev * 10 + (n MOD 10)
  SET n = n DIV 10
ENDWHILE
PRINT rev
